questions.prompt: Match each part of a Sequential Function Chart to what it means.

pairs.right: A step: active while the machine is in it

pairs.left: A box with a double border
pairs.right: The initial step: active when the PLC starts

pairs.left: A bar across the line, with a condition

pairs.right: An action: what the step does

questions.explanation: Steps are boxes, the initial step has a double border, transitions are bars with conditions, and actions sit beside their steps.

options: When the step before it is active AND its condition is TRUE
Whenever its condition is TRUE, whichever step is active
When the step after it is active AND its condition is TRUE
Once in every scan, whatever its condition and the steps say
questions.explanation: A transition belongs to the step before it. BasketIsDown means nothing in step S3; it moves the chart on only while S1 is active.

questions.prompt: In the parts washer's chart, S2 (wash) is active and the wash time is up (WashTimer.Q is TRUE). What happens?
options: S2 goes inactive and S3 (raise the basket) goes active
S3 (raise the basket) goes active, and S2 stays active too
Nothing yet: S2 stays active until Start is pressed again
S2 goes inactive and the chart goes back to S0 (idle)
questions.explanation: The transition below S2 is WashTimer.Q. It fires: the step before it ends and the step after it starts, in the same moment.

questions.prompt: An action in step S1 has the qualifier **N**. When is it on?
options: While S1 is active, and off as soon as S1 ends
From S1 on, and it stays on until a reset action turns it off
For one scan only, at the moment S1 becomes active
Once S1 has been active for a set time, until S1 ends
questions.explanation: N (non-stored) is the usual action: on exactly while its step is active, like a coil driven by the step's bit. S stays on, P pulses once, D waits.

questions.prompt: A chart splits on a **double** line into two paths: one fills a tank while the other heats an oven. What does that mean?
options: Both paths run at the same time, and the chart goes on only when both are done and meet again at a double line
Only one path is taken, the first whose transition comes true, and the other is skipped
Both paths run, one after the other: the left path first, then the right when it is done
It is a drawing mistake: a chart cannot split, so the tool refuses to run it
questions.explanation: A double line is a simultaneous (parallel) branch: every path runs. A single line is a selection: one path is chosen.

questions.prompt: You write the washer's chart in ladder with one BOOL per step, S0 to S4. How do you make S0 the **initial** step?
options: Give S0 a starting value of TRUE, so it is active when the PLC starts
Put S0's rung last, so it is the step left active at the end of the first scan
Put S0's rung first, so it is the first step the PLC runs when it starts
Nothing: every BOOL starts TRUE, so S0 is already active when the PLC starts
questions.explanation: BOOL tags start FALSE unless they are given a starting value. The program on the Example tab declares S0 with the starting value TRUE. With a step number, step 0 is the initial step, because an INT starts at 0.

questions.prompt: In the ladder version of the washer's chart, step S3's rung starts S3 from the step before AND a condition. Type the **step before** S3 (such as S1).
questions.explanation: S3 (raise the basket) comes after S2 (wash): its rung starts it from S2 AND WashTimer.Q, the transition between them.
